returns.maxAge: The oldest feed answer accepted, in seconds.
returns.boundBp: The most a sale may lose against the feed, in basis points.

exitStep.does: Unwinds the Aave position and sends the proceeds to the hub, which pays the owner's withdrawal address. Each part runs on its own so that one that fails (a paused reserve, no flash liquidity, a pool away from the oracle, a stale price) logs `ExitPartFailed` and the others still run. First, when the contract holds the pinned reward (ARB or aArbARB, at least 0.01) or has aArbARB on as collateral, the reward parts: turn aArbARB's collateral off, then sell the reward for USDC, each with its own gas cap. Then: repay the debt with the USDC held (including what the hub sent it in exit), then with the USDC supplied (aUSDC), then with collateral through the repay-with-collateral contract or, if that fails, by withdrawing what Aave lets go, selling and repaying; once the debt is zero, withdraw the the asset and the USDC supplied, each as far as Aave holds it; sell the the asset held; send the USDC held to the hub, less what still repays a debt. A sale may fill in part: what the price band does not let it sell waits for a later call. Counted in `opCount`.
exitStep.who: Anyone, as often as needed: it takes no recipient and pays only the hub.
exitStep.when: Only in exit, until nothing is left.
checks: Called on a strategy's own contract, never on the module or the leg code directly.
The contract is in exit.

With reward work, the call reverts `GasTooLow` unless it carries enough gas for both reward parts' caps and the position's parts: the reward is never skipped silently. Whether there is reward work is read with capped calls; a reward token that fails to answer counts as none.

Every the asset sale in exit fills only at pool prices no worse than Aave's oracle less 50 bp (less when the owner signed an oracle bound under 55 bp: the bound less the pool's 0.05 % fee), so a caller who moves the pool first can't make it sell cheaper; the pool already below that price, the part sells nothing (`PoolOffOracle`). Its average must still reach the oracle less the oracle bound, on what it sold.

The repay with collateral, whose sale runs inside the repay-with-collateral contract, reads the pool's price before (`PoolOffOracle`) and after (`BandCrossed`: the chunk was too big for the band, nothing is repaid); `debtChunk` sizes it. With `debtChunk` 0 a debt larger than the band holds goes to the fallback, which makes progress while the health factor is above 1 and AAVE has the asset to lend out; otherwise a smaller `debtChunk` on the repay with collateral is the way forward.

The fallback withdraws at most the collateral Aave lets go (the liquidation-weighted collateral above the debt, less 1 %, as if the the asset withdrawn counted in full, so never more than Aave allows whatever other collateral is held) and what the reserve holds, sells what the band allows, supplies the rest back, repays, and leaves the health factor no lower than before.
The reward sale in exit fills only at prices no worse than Chainlink's ARB / USD less 50 bp, its average at least that value less 1 % on what it sold. Outside the exit the key's sales are unchanged.
While a debt stands, the USDC sent to the hub leaves on the contract its debt and a small headroom (10 bp and 1 USDC), so USDC the hub sent to repay the debt never goes back.
A reward part keeps at most 256 bytes of its revert data in `ExitPartFailed`. The daily loss budget does not apply in exit.

The payment to the hub never reverts: on the same chain it is a transfer whose failure is ignored; across chains a standard Circle burn bound to the hub, skipped while Circle's minimum fee is above 10 bp or Circle refuses it.

params.debtChunk: The most debt to repay with collateral in this call, in USDC's smallest unit (6 decimals); 0 repays all of it, or, when that is more than the price band holds, leaves it to the fallback.
params.assetChunk: The most the asset to sell in this call, in wei (18 decimals); 0 sells all of it, as far as the price band allows.

exitPart.does: Runs one part of `exitStep`, so that it can fail on its own: 1 repays with the USDC held; 2 repays with the aUSDC held (Aave's `repayWithATokens`); 3 repays with collateral through the repay-with-collateral contract, the pool's price read before and after; 4 repays by withdrawing what Aave lets go, selling it within the band, supplying back what was not sold and repaying; 5 withdraws the the asset supplied once the debt is zero, as far as the reserve holds it; 10 does the same for the USDC supplied; 6 sells the the asset held for USDC within the band; 7 sends the USDC held to the hub, less the debt and its headroom while one stands; 8 sells the pinned reward held (ARB, and aArbARB withdrawn), nothing under 0.01; 9 turns aArbARB's collateral off when it is on.
exitPart.who: This contract only, calling itself from `exitStep`.
checks: The caller is this contract itself.
Parts 1 to 4 do nothing once the debt is zero, and parts 5 and 10 nothing while there is debt.

Parts 3 and 4 spend at most the collateral bound for the chunk of debt (its value at Aave's oracle plus the oracle bound), and never more the aToken than is held; part 4 at most the liquidation-weighted collateral above the debt, less 1 %, and what the the asset reserve holds.
Parts 3, 4 and 6 refuse a pool already at or below the band's limit (`PoolOffOracle`); part 3 refuses a repay that left the pool below it (`BandCrossed`).
Part 4 reverts if the health factor ends lower than before, or if Aave refuses to take back the unsold the asset.

params.part: Which part to run, 1 to 10 (9 and 8 run first, when there is reward work; 10 after 5).
params.arg: For parts 3 and 4, the most debt to repay (USDC, 6 decimals; 0 all of it); for part 6, the most the asset to sell (18 decimals; 0 all of it); unused by the other parts.

exitDebt.does: In exit, the USDC this contract owes and can't repay from its own USDC and aUSDC, plus 10 bp of it and 1 USDC of headroom for the interest that accrues before its next `exitStep`; zero when it owes nothing uncovered, and zero outside the exit. The hub beside it sends it at most this, before paying the owner (amendment 2d). In USDC, 6 decimals. Zero, too, while the position is insolvent: its the asset at Aave's oracle worth less than its debt (USDC at $1), read without Aave's loop over every reserve, so no stranger's dust can push the hub's capped read out of gas. That debt is Aave's liquidators' to write off, never the owner's cash to repay.

receiveMint.does: Completes a Circle CCTP V2 mint of USDC bound to this contract and counts it: a burn by another contract of the strategy, from its own chain, adds to what was received from that contract and to Circle's fees on it; any other burn is accepted and counted apart.
receiveMint.who: Anyone: the mint can only pay this contract.
receiveMint.when: In any state, the exit included.
checks: The message is a burn to this chain, addressed to this chain's Circle TokenMessenger, with this contract as both the mint's recipient and the only caller allowed to complete it.
Circle's transmitter checks the attestation and that the message is used once.
Exactly the amount burned less Circle's fee arrived.

params.message: The CCTP V2 message Circle attested: a USDC burn whose recipient and destination caller are this contract.

report.does: Sends this leg's report to its hub: its holdings, the USDC sent to and received from each contract of the strategy, Circle's fees on what it received, a sequence number, and the time and block they were read in. The hub uses it to value the strategy.
report.who: Anyone: it reports to the hub only.
checks: Every figure is read in this one block.
On the hub's chain the hub takes it directly; on another chain it goes as a Circle message at finalized finality, and the call reverts if Circle refuses it.

holdings.does: The report's figures as a view, so that a hub on the same chain can read them without a message. The holdings are two: `ETH`, the the aToken and the asset held, and `USD`, the USDC and aUSDC held less the variable USDC debt, both signed and in 18 decimals.

returns.1: The leg's holdings now, each an asset and an amount, as its report to the hub carries them.
returns.2: What this contract has sent to each other contract of the strategy, gross, by link (0 the hub).
returns.3: What it has received from each other contract of the strategy, gross, by link.
returns.4: The block number of this reading.
returns.5: The block of its last move between HyperEVM and HyperCore (0 for a leg with none).
returns.6: How many counted calls it has made (`opCount`): the hub sees a move between two readings.
returns.7: Whether every change of its holdings goes through its own counted calls, so the hub may read it alone.

scheduleUpgrade.does: Schedules the strategy's upgrade to the version whose manifest the owner signed (`UpgradeStrategy(hub, chainId, manifest, nonce, deadline)`): the hub's code moves 24 hours later, its legs follow. A leg refuses it (`Unsupported`): the hub is the strategy's home.
scheduleUpgrade.who: The owner, by one credential's signature; anyone may submit it.
scheduleUpgrade.when: Any time, an exit included; refused while any action (an upgrade or a profile switch) is pending.
checks: The signature is the named credential's, at its own vault nonce, before the deadline (`BadSignature`, `Expired`).
The manifest is listed on this chain's registry at a version above the hub's, with a hub implementation (`NotListed`).
No action is pending (`AlreadyPending`), and the credential's removal is not pending (`RemovalPending`).

params.manifest: The version's manifest: the keccak of every member type's (type, domain, implementation, code hash) in it, the same bytes on every chain.
params.credential: The signing credential's id, `keccak256(abi.encode(kind, x, y))` as the deposit contract keys it: it must be the credential that signed, and its own vault nonce is spent.
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds.
params.signature: One owner credential's signature, in the deposit contract's "DLTX Owner" domain (no chain id): `0x01 ‖ r ‖ s ‖ v` for a wallet, or `0x02 ‖ x ‖ y ‖` the ABI-encoded WebAuthn assertion for a passkey.

cancelPendingAction.does: Cancels the pending upgrade or profile switch it names, exactly (`CancelPendingAction(hub, chainId, kind, target, due, deadline)`). A leg refuses it (`Unsupported`): the hub is the strategy's home.
cancelPendingAction.who: Any credential of the owner in effect; no nonce. Anyone may submit it.
cancelPendingAction.when: Until the action is applied, after its due time included.
checks: One credential in effect signed it, before the deadline.
An action of that kind, target and due time is pending (`NotPending`).

params.target: What it names: the version's manifest, or the profile.
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds.
params.signature: One owner credential's signature, in the deposit contract's "DLTX Owner" domain (no chain id): `0x01 ‖ r ‖ s ‖ v` for a wallet, or `0x02 ‖ x ‖ y ‖` the ABI-encoded WebAuthn assertion for a passkey.

applyUpgrade.does: Applies the due upgrade: the hub's code moves to the version's hub implementation, then it tells every leg (the one beside it by a direct `followUpgrade`, the one on another chain by Circle). Nothing else moves: no money, no position, no fee. A leg refuses it (`Unsupported`): the hub is the strategy's home.
applyUpgrade.when: Once the upgrade is due, outside the money lock; allowed during an exit.
checks: An upgrade is pending (`NotPending`) and due (`NotDue`).
Its scheduling credential still stands in the deposit contract and has no removal pending: otherwise the schedule is cleared instead (`ActionCleared`).
A leg on another chain that Circle cannot reach now is logged (`UpgradePending`): `publishUpgrade` resends it.

publishUpgrade.does: Sends the hub's current manifest, with a fresh publication time, to leg `k`: a leg created after its hub moved, or whose message expired or met a version its chain had not listed yet, catches up. A leg refuses it (`Unsupported`): the hub is the strategy's home.
publishUpgrade.when: Any time. Reverts as Circle (or the leg) does.

params.k: The leg, by its index among the hub's links.

followUpgrade.does: A leg on the hub's chain follows the hub's upgrade: it resolves the manifest on its own chain's registry and moves to that version's implementation of its member type; a version not above its own is ignored.
followUpgrade.who: The strategy's hub beside it (its link 0, on this chain), in the transaction that moved it.
checks: The caller is this leg's link 0 on this chain (`NotAllowed`).
The manifest is listed on this chain (`NotListed`).

followMessage.does: A leg on another chain than its hub follows the hub's `.upgrade.v1` message: ignored when published before this leg's creation, at or before its last applied upgrade, or more than 3 days ago; otherwise it resolves the manifest on this chain's registry and moves to that version's implementation (a manifest not listed here reverts, so the message waits, relayable).
followMessage.who: Circle's message transmitter, delivering the hub's finalized message (any other caller is refused).

pendingAction.does: The pending action: its kind (0 none, 1 an upgrade, 2 a profile switch), due time, scheduling credential and target.

returns.kind: 0 none, 1 an upgrade, 2 a profile switch.

MEMBER_TYPE.does: This implementation's member type: 1 the hub, 2 the Aave V3 asset leg, 3 the Hyperliquid leg.

exitModule.does: The exit module this leg runs by DELEGATECALL (`AaveV3AssetLegExit`), its code hash checked when the implementation was deployed.

rewardsModule.does: The rewards module this leg runs by DELEGATECALL (`AaveV3AssetLegRewards`), its code hash checked when the implementation was deployed.

profile.does: The asset profile this leg holds now: written at creation and by a profile switch only.

assetProfile.does: The stored asset profile: the asset is read here, never from the code.

returns.assetIsToken0: Whether the asset is the pool's token0.
returns.holdingAsset: The holding's id in a report.
returns.rateFeed: A wrapped asset's market-rate feed, zero for none.

checkProfile.does: The long's part of an asset profile, checked on this chain when the registry accepts it (AP-3): the token's decimals (6 to 18) and order against USDC, its aToken Aave's, its pool the receiver's router's factory's for (token, USDC, fee); the reserve active, not frozen, not paused, a base LTV above zero, no debt ceiling, virtual accounting; Aave's oracle a source and a positive price; the token neither USDC, nor the reward, nor its own aToken; the bound's floor above the pool's fee; the rate feed's `description()` the profile's and a fresh positive answer; the short's asset derived from the perp's coin. Reverts `BadProfile` otherwise.

checkAtCreation.does: The same checks again at this leg's creation, the reserve's state included, but not the rate feed's liveness (a creation never waits for a feed).
checkAtCreation.who: The leg itself, from its initialisation.

params.p: The profile, as stored in the registry.

followSwitch.does: Follows the owner's profile switch: the leg's route (pool, fee tier, token order, rate feed, the bound's floor) becomes the new profile's, its facts on this chain checked again by this version's code (the rate feed's liveness aside). Counted, so a fee snapshot taken before it is refused.
followSwitch.who: The hub beside it (its link 0, on this chain), applying the switch.
followSwitch.when: Outside the exit and this leg's money lock.
checks: The caller is the hub beside it (`NotAllowed`).
The profile is open here, of the same token, aToken, decimals and holding, and the signed `oracleBoundBp` is at least its floor and above its pool's fee (`BadProfile`).

rewardPart.does: The exit's reward parts, run from `exitStep` under its lock and gas cap: 9 switches aArbARB's collateral off, 8 sells the reward held (within the band in exit).
rewardPart.who: The leg itself, from its exit.

Swapped.does: A sale on the pinned Uniswap V3 pool: by `swap`, or one of the exit's sales.

params.amountIn: What the pool took, in the token's smallest unit (18 decimals for the asset, 6 for USDC).
params.amountOut: What the pool paid, in the other token's smallest unit.
params.lossUsd: What the sale lost against Aave's oracle, in USD with 8 decimals; 0 if none. Charged to the loss budget outside the exit.
params.assetToUsdc: True for a sale of the asset, false for a purchase.

RepaidWithCollateral.does: Debt was repaid with collateral through the repay-with-collateral contract: by `repayWithCollateral`, or in the exit.

params.debtRepaid: How much the variable USDC debt fell, in its smallest unit (6 decimals).
params.collateralOut: The collateral spent: the the aToken that left less any the asset handed back, in wei (18 decimals).
params.lossUsd: What the repayment lost against Aave's oracle, in USD with 8 decimals; 0 if none. Charged to the loss budget outside the exit.

ExitPartFailed.does: One part of `exitStep` failed; the other parts still ran.

params.reason: The part's revert data (at most 256 bytes for the reward parts 8 and 9).

RewardClaimed.does: A claim of this contract's (`claimRewards`, `claimMerkl`) delivered the pinned reward. A claim made for this contract by a third party at Merkl's distributor emits no `RewardClaimed`; Merkl's own `Claimed` records it.

params.gained: The ARB and aArbARB this contract gained in the claim, in 18 decimals.

RewardSwapped.does: A sale of the pinned reward on the ARB/USDC pool: by `swapReward`, or the exit's part 8.

params.rewardIn: The ARB the pool took, in 18 decimals.
params.usdcOut: The USDC it paid, in 6 decimals.
params.lossUsd: What the sale lost against Chainlink's ARB / USD, in USD with 8 decimals; 0 if none. Counted in the loss budget outside the exit, never refused by it.

UpgradeSent.does: The hub told leg `link` of its version (directly beside it, or by Circle).

UpgradePending.does: The hub could not tell leg `link` now (Circle refused, or the leg is not yet created): `publishUpgrade` resends it.

ProfileFollowed.does: The leg followed a profile switch.

errors.BadAsset: `withdraw` was asked for a token other than the asset or USDC.
errors.BelowHealthFloor: A borrow, a withdrawal or an e-mode change would leave Aave's health factor below the health floor.
errors.HealthFell: A repay with collateral, or the exit's repay by sale, left Aave's health factor lower than before.
errors.AboveBound: A repay with collateral offered more collateral than the oracle bound allows for the debt, or lost more than the oracle bound of the collateral's value.
errors.OverBudget: A sale's loss against Aave's oracle, or a Circle fee on `send`, would take the losses counted today and yesterday above the daily loss budget of the position's equity. A reward sale is counted in the budget but never refused by it.
errors.SwapShort: The pool paid less than the minimum out, raised to the oracle bound.
errors.BadParams: A configuration names protocols other than the pinned ones, or numbers outside this leg's bounds.
errors.RewardCollateralOn: `swapReward` was called while aArbARB is enabled as Aave collateral on this contract: `rewardCollateralOff` first.
errors.StalePrice: Chainlink's ARB / USD answer is older than 25 hours or not positive, or Arbitrum's sequencer is down or restarted within the hour: the reward is not sold.
errors.PoolOffOracle: In exit, the pool's price is already at or below the band's limit (Aave's oracle less 50 bp, or the reward's feed less 50 bp): nothing is sold in this part until arbitrage brings the pool back.
errors.BandCrossed: In exit, the repay with collateral's own sale left the pool below the band's limit: the chunk of debt was too big for the band, and nothing was repaid. A smaller `debtChunk` goes through.

contracts.name: HyperCoreLeg
contracts.title: The short contract, version 1
contracts.brief: A strategy's Hyperliquid account on HyperEVM, its perp the profile's, owner-upgradeable.
contracts.summary: Version 1 of the short contract: the same Hyperliquid account on HyperEVM (an agent trades it, DLTX's execution key moves its margin and reduces with reduce-only orders, money goes only to the strategy's other contracts), behind a fixed proxy whose code moves only when its hub's owner-signed upgrade reaches it. Its perp, the perp's coin and its asset id are its asset profile's, checked against HyperCore at creation: the asset id is derived from the coin, so a perp can never report as another asset. Its exit runs in two modules, `HyperCoreLegExit` and `HyperCoreLegExitB`; its upgrade path in the shared `VaultUpgrade`.

legInfo.does: Describes this leg code to the combination factory, which checks its pins against it.

returns.roles: The roles this leg may take, one bit each: 3, both long (1) and short (2).
returns.valueKind: How its value is known: 1, read on chain (the hub may value it from figures the contract reads itself).

paramsType.does: This leg's parameters as the owner signs them in `CreateVault`: the typed-data struct `HyperCoreLeg(uint32 perp,bytes32 asset,uint16 orderBoundBp,uint16 fastFeeCapBp,uint16 feeBudgetBp)`, named by the leg type, which may play either role. The combination factory checks it against its pin on HyperEVM. Returns the struct's type string.

validateParams.does: Checks a short contract's parameters before the combination factory creates one with them; reverts with `BadParams` when they are out of bounds, returns nothing otherwise.
checks: The perp is one of Hyperliquid's own perps (DEX 0), an index under 10,000.
The asset is named and is not USD.
The order bound is 30 to 1,000 bp.
The fast-fee cap is at most 50 bp.
The fee budget is 1 to 500 bp.

params.r: The combination factory's registry (this chain's), whose open asset profiles the parameters are checked against: an implementation names no registry (version 1's are the registry's genesis).
params.params: The ABI-encoded `ShortParams`: the perp's index, its asset as the hub values it, the order bound, the fast-fee cap and the fee budget, all in bp.

receive.does: Accepts HYPE on HyperEVM, and only from Hyperliquid's HYPE system address: HYPE coming back from this account's HyperCore balance.
receive.who: Only `HYPE_SYSTEM`; any other sender reverts. To bring HYPE in, call `topUpHype` with it.

toMargin.does: Deposits USDC this contract holds on HyperEVM into its own perp margin on HyperCore, through Circle's CoreDepositWallet. The first deposit creates the contract's HyperCore account.
toMargin.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.

params.amount: The USDC to deposit (6 decimals).

fromMargin.does: Brings USDC back from HyperCore to this contract on HyperEVM, in two HyperCore actions: perp margin to spot, then spot to HyperEVM. HyperCore carries them out after the transaction; one it refuses does not revert this call.
fromMargin.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
fromMargin.when: Outside the exit. The second action's fee is paid in HYPE from the account's spot balance, so it needs a little HYPE there (`topUpHype`). The account's first outgoing USDC transfer also pays about 1 USDC from spot on top of the amount; on a first call with no other USDC on spot, HyperCore drops the second action silently and the amount stays on spot. `prime` pays that fee first.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.

params.amount: The USDC to bring back (6 decimals).

prime.does: Pays the account's first-transfer fee, about 1 USDC in USDC, which HyperCore charges on an account's first outgoing USDC transfer and which `fromMargin` cannot pay on a fresh account: it moves 1.2 USDC of perp margin to spot, then sends 0.05 USDC from spot to this contract on HyperEVM, so the amount and the fee fit. About 0.145 USDC stays on spot. In unified mode the first action may do nothing; spot is then the whole balance and pays. HyperCore carries both out after the transaction; one it refuses does not revert this call. Calling it again is harmless: the money stays in the account. Counted in `opCount`.
prime.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
prime.when: Outside the exit, once at custody creation, with HYPE on the account's spot for the second action's fee.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.

topUpHype.does: Sends HYPE from HyperEVM to this account's HyperCore spot balance, where it pays the fees of transfers out of HyperCore.
topUpHype.who: The execution key, while not revoked; in exit, anyone.
topUpHype.when: Any time; the exit needs it when `exitStatus` raises flag 2.
checks: Outside the exit, the caller is the group's execution key and the owner has not revoked it.
The transfer to `HYPE_SYSTEM` succeeds: the contract holds at least `amount`, the HYPE sent with the call included.

params.amount: The HYPE to send, in HyperEVM's units (18 decimals). It may be brought with the call.

send.does: Sends USDC from this contract on HyperEVM to another member of the strategy: its hub or a sister leg. On the same chain it is a transfer the receiver pulls; across chains, a Circle burn whose mint only the receiver can complete.
send.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
send.when: Outside the exit, once the receiver is ready (`ready(k)`).
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.
The amount is not zero, and member `k` is ready: its `READY` message arrived, or, on this chain, its code is there.
Across chains, Circle's minimum fee is at most 10 bp of the amount.
At fast finality, `maxFee` is at most `fastFeeCapBp` of the amount; it is raised to Circle's minimum if lower. At standard finality the fee is Circle's minimum alone.

The fee, added to what was charged today and yesterday (UTC days), stays within `feeBudgetBp` of the account's value read before the call: DEX 0's account value (never below zero), spot USDC and the USDC held on HyperEVM. In both of Hyperliquid's account modes this counts the perp's margin once: in unified mode HyperCore's spot balance is what is available, the margin staying in DEX 0's account value.

params.k: The receiving member, by its link index here: 0 is the hub, then the sister legs.
params.amount: The USDC to send (6 decimals).
params.fast: Whether to ask Circle for a fast transfer (confirmed finality, with a fee) rather than a standard one (finalized).
params.maxFee: The most Circle may take on a fast transfer, in USDC (6 decimals); ignored at standard finality.

order.does: Places this account's own order on the strategy's perp: immediate-or-cancel, reduce-only, at Hyperliquid's oracle price moved by the order bound against the trade. Growing the position is the agent's work alone.
order.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.
`reduceOnly` is true.

params.isBuy: True to buy (reduce a short), false to sell (reduce a long).
params.sz: The size, in 1e8 × the asset's units.
params.reduceOnly: Must be true: any other value reverts.

cancel.does: Cancels a resting order of this account on HyperCore.
cancel.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.

params.asset: The order's market, by Hyperliquid's asset id.
params.byCloid: True when `id` is the order's client id, false when it is Hyperliquid's order id.
params.id: The client id (128 bits), or Hyperliquid's order id (its low 64 bits).

proposeAgent.does: Proposes DLTX's agent for this account: the key that trades it on Hyperliquid: it cannot withdraw to an outside address, but it can trade at a loss. It replaces any earlier proposal. The account's first agent may be applied at once; any later one after 24 hours, unless the owner cancels it.
proposeAgent.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.
`next` is not the zero address.

applyAgent.does: Makes DLTX's proposed agent the account's agent on HyperCore, replacing the previous one.
applyAgent.who: The execution key, while not revoked.
applyAgent.when: Outside the exit; at once for the account's first agent, otherwise 24 hours after the proposal.
checks: The caller is the group's execution key in the registry, the owner has not revoked it, and the contract is not in exit.
An agent is proposed.
If an agent was ever set, 24 hours have passed since the proposal.
The contract's HyperCore account exists (its first deposit made it).

applyOwnerAgent.does: Makes the agent the owner chose (other than the burner) the account's agent on HyperCore, once the choice has stood 24 hours. In exit, it also becomes the agent the exit keeps re-approving.
applyOwnerAgent.when: In any state, 24 hours after the owner's choice, unless an owner credential cancelled it, and only while the credential that chose it is still one in this chain's owner record: removing a stolen credential voids its pending choice.
checks: The owner has an agent pending.
24 hours have passed since the owner chose it.

The credential that signed the choice is still a credential in effect in the deposit contract's record on this chain (`isCredentialId`); otherwise it reverts (`NotAllowed`). An unsynced copy has no credential, so it reverts there too until the record arrives again.

burner.does: The burner agent: an address derived from this contract's address, whose key nobody holds. Making it the agent stops all trading at once; the exit begins with it, and the owner may name it with immediate effect.

USDC.does: Circle's USDC on HyperEVM (6 decimals): the only token the strategy's contracts move between them.

CORE_DEPOSIT_WALLET.does: Circle's CoreDepositWallet on HyperEVM: a deposit there credits the caller's perp margin on HyperCore.

HYPE_SYSTEM.does: Hyperliquid's HYPE system address: HYPE sent to it on HyperEVM credits the sender's HyperCore spot balance, and HYPE coming back from HyperCore arrives from it.

USDC_SYSTEM.does: Hyperliquid's USDC system address: HyperCore USDC sent to it, spot to spot, returns Circle USDC to the sender on HyperEVM.

NOT_IN_EXIT.does: `exitStatus`'s state when the contract is not in exit.

CLOSING.does: `exitStatus`'s state while the exit still has something to close, move or sell.

RECOVERED.does: `exitStatus`'s state once everything has left the account, with no residue.

RECOVERED_WITH_RESIDUE.does: `exitStatus`'s state once everything the exit can move has left, with a pinned token left over too small to sell: only then may `sweepResidue` send it to an owner wallet.

perp.does: The strategy's perp: its index among Hyperliquid's own perps (DEX 0), for example 1 for ETH. Fixed at creation.

orderBoundBp.does: The bound on every price this contract sets, in bp: its own orders and the exit's closes at Hyperliquid's oracle price moved by it against the trade, the exit's HYPE purchases and sales, and the book price that tightens an owner's order. Fixed at creation.

fastFeeCapBp.does: The most a fast transfer by `send` may pay Circle, in bp of the amount. Fixed at creation.

feeBudgetBp.does: The most Circle's fees on this contract's transfers may total in any 24 hours, in bp of the account's value read before each transfer. Fixed at creation.

asset.does: The perp's asset as the hub values it in this leg's reports (for example `keccak256("dltx.asset.ETH")`). Fixed at creation.

lastCoreMove.does: The block of the last move between HyperEVM and HyperCore that this contract started (`toMargin`, `fromMargin`, the exit's transfer out of spot). Its reports carry it, since HyperCore credits such a move a block or two later.

agent.does: The agent this contract last approved on HyperCore (zero before the first).

pendingAgent.does: DLTX's proposed agent, waiting for `applyAgent` (zero if none). Revoking the execution key, the owner's agent actions and the exit clear it.

pendingAgentAt.does: When DLTX's agent was proposed, as a Unix time in seconds.

agentEverSet.does: Whether an agent has ever been approved: until then DLTX's first proposal applies at once.

ownerAgent.does: The agent the owner chose other than the burner, waiting for its 24 hours (zero if none).

ownerAgentAt.does: When the owner chose that agent, as a Unix time in seconds.

exitAgent.does: The agent the exit keeps re-approving: the burner from the moment the exit begins, or the owner's own agent once applied in exit (zero before the exit).

purchases.does: How many times the exit has bought HYPE for transfer fees: at most three.

marginTriedAt.does: The block of the exit's first try to move DEX 0's margin to spot; zero before. In budget mode, two pacing windows after it the floor is fixed even if the margin never moved (unified mode).

floorSet.does: Whether the exit has fixed its spot floor `floor` (budget mode).

floor.does: Budget mode: the spot USDC the exit keeps, `R` (1.1 times the larger of the dropped-out position's margin and 10% of its notional) plus 1.05 USDC for the first-transfer fee, fixed once. What is above it and the reservation may leave spot, later arrivals included. In HyperCore's USDC units (8 decimals).

reserved.does: Budget mode: USDC sent from spot to HyperEVM and not yet seen arriving there, in HyperCore's USDC units (8 decimals). It is released only once as much USDC from outside the strategy (Circle's mints from members set aside) has arrived on HyperEVM since the first of these sends, never by time alone; or by the owner's signed action 5 (`ownerAction`), when a send will not execute.

dexSince.does: When a HIP-3 DEX joined the exit's watched list, as a Unix time in seconds; zero if it is not watched.

lastSent.does: The block at which the exit last sent a paced action, by the action's key (its kind and its market or token). An action sent in the last 20 blocks is not sent again.

sweepSince.does: When `proposeSweep` first saw an address as an owner wallet credential on this chain, as a Unix time in seconds; zero if never.

exitStep.does: Drives the exit on HyperCore: it reads the account and sends every action the state still calls for, then sends the USDC this contract holds on HyperEVM to its hub. Each action is safe to repeat; one sent in the last 20 blocks is not sent again. Call it until `exitStatus` reads recovered.
exitStep.when: In exit, as often as needed.
checks: The contract is in exit.

It re-approves the exit's agent, cancels the resting orders named, and adds each HIP-3 DEX named to the watched list when it can be read and holds a position or at least 1 USD (at most 16; when full, a DEX left with no position and at most 0.01 USD gives its place).

It closes each open position on DEX 0, the strategy's perp and every perp named: reduce-only, immediate-or-cancel, its whole size, at the oracle price moved by the order bound. A named perp index of 10,000 or more reverts.
Nothing leaves spot in a call that has a DEX 0 position open, nor while DEX 0 or a watched DEX in its first 7 days shows a position (or, for a watched DEX, cannot be read).

Otherwise it moves DEX 0's withdrawable margin and each flat watched DEX's balance to spot, buys HYPE for fees if spot HYPE is under 0.0002 (the fewest 0.01 steps worth Hyperliquid's 10 USDC order minimum, at most three times), sends spot USDC to HyperEVM once HYPE is there (the balance read; when the read has not fallen since the last such send, which may have been dropped for want of the account's first-transfer fee of about 1 USDC, the balance less 1.05 USDC, so the fee fits), and sells HYPE above 0.0002 and the pinned stablecoins (USDE, USDT0, USDH at 1 USD less the bound) when a sale is worth at least 10 USDC.

A watched DEX still showing a position after 7 days stops holding the rest back (budget mode): from then spot keeps a floor, fixed once DEX 0's margin is on spot: 1.1 times the larger of that position's margin and 10% of its notional, plus 1.05 USDC for the first-transfer fee. What is above the floor and the reservation may leave or be spent, later arrivals on spot included. Each send to HyperEVM is reserved until as much USDC from outside the strategy has arrived there, so a send HyperCore drops is never counted as gone; a send that will never execute stays reserved until the owner's signed action 5. The stablecoins are not sold meanwhile.

Last, the USDC held on HyperEVM goes to the hub: a transfer on the same chain, else a Circle burn at standard finality whose mint only the hub can complete, at Circle's minimum fee; skipped, never a revert, if that fee is above 10 bp or Circle refuses.

params.a: What the caller names, since no precompile lists it (`ExitArgs`): resting orders to cancel, DEX 0 perps holding a position besides the strategy's own, and HIP-3 DEXes to watch, each with the collateral token its balance is moved to spot in.

bridgeOut.does: Sends the USDC this contract holds on HyperEVM to its hub, with no HyperCore read, so it works even when a read of HyperCore fails: a transfer on the same chain, else a Circle burn at standard finality whose mint only the hub can complete. Skipped, never a revert, if Circle's minimum fee is above 10 bp or Circle refuses.

ownerOrder.does: Places the owner's own order at the owner's limit, for what the exit cannot close alone: a HIP-3 position, a token with no independent price, or a DEX 0 position that will not fill within the bound. Immediate-or-cancel; reduce-only on a perp; a sale only on spot. A HIP-3 order's DEX joins the watched list.
ownerOrder.who: Anyone may submit it, with one owner credential's signature.
checks: The contract is in exit.
The asset is a DEX 0 perp, a spot market or a HIP-3 perp; `szDecimals` is at most 6 for a perp and 8 for spot; a spot order is a sale.

The deadline has not passed, and the owner's deposit contract on this chain accepts the signature of the `OwnerOrder` message, which names this contract, the chain, every order field, the signing credential's next nonce on this contract (`ownerNonceOf(credential)`; the credential named must be the one that made the signature) and the deadline. That credential's nonce then advances.
The limit is tightened, never loosened, by the book: a buy pays at most the best offer plus the order bound, a sale gets at least the best bid less it. With no book the owner's limit stands.

params.asset: Hyperliquid's asset id: a DEX 0 perp (under 10,000), a spot market (10,000 plus its index) or a HIP-3 perp (100,000 plus 10,000 × its DEX plus its index).
params.isBuy: True to buy (a perp only: it reduces a short), false to sell.
params.size: The size, in 1e8 × the asset's units.
params.limitPx: The owner's limit price, in 1e8 × the price in USD; it must be a price Hyperliquid accepts.
params.szDecimals: The asset's size decimals on Hyperliquid, used to read the book's price and round the bound.
params.credential: The signing credential's id in the deposit contract (`credentialId`), whose nonce the signature carries.
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds: the call reverts after it.
params.signature: One owner credential's signature over the EIP-712 `OwnerOrder` message, in the owner's domain, verified by the deposit contract.

proposeSweep.does: Starts the 24 hours an owner wallet must stand before the residue may be swept to it: it records the first time it sees `to` as a wallet credential in this chain's copy of the owner record. A later call for the same address changes nothing.
checks: The contract is in exit.
`to` is a wallet credential of the owner on this chain.

params.to: The owner wallet that may later receive the residue.

sweepResidue.does: Sends a pinned token's residue, the amount `exitStatus` lists, from this account's HyperCore spot balance to an owner wallet on HyperCore. Never USDC; it is not a withdrawal: its destination and amount are fixed. If the account never paid its first-transfer fee (about 1 USDC, from spot USDC), HyperCore drops it silently; an exit send that landed, or custody creation's move, has paid it.
sweepResidue.when: In exit, once `exitStatus` reads recovered with residue.
checks: The contract is in exit and its state is recovered with residue.
`token` is a pinned token (HYPE, USDE, USDT0, USDH) with a residue listed.
`proposeSweep` saw `to` at least 24 hours ago, and it is still a wallet credential of the owner on this chain.
The same token was not swept in the last 20 blocks.

params.token: The pinned token's HyperCore id: HYPE 150, USDE 235, USDT0 268, USDH 360.
params.to: The owner wallet to receive it.

exitStatus.does: The exit's progress, from reads alone. Outside the exit, the state is 0 and only flag 32 can be set.

returns.state: 0 not in exit, 1 closing, 2 recovered, 3 recovered with residue.
returns.dexes: The watched HIP-3 DEXes (DEX 0 is always watched).
returns.residue: What is left of each pinned token, in order HYPE, USDE, USDT0, USDH, in the token's HyperCore units (8 decimals): HYPE above the 0.0002 kept for fees, each listed when worth at least 0.01 USD.
returns.flags: Bits: 1 a member not yet told of the exit (`notifyLink`); 2 needs HYPE for fees (spot USDC under 11, or three purchases spent: `topUpHype`); 4 budget mode (a watched DEX kept a position past 7 days: spot keeps `floor`, and sends not yet seen arriving stay `reserved`); 8 waiting for the owner (a watched DEX shows a position or cannot be read); 16 margin held while flat (perhaps an unnamed resting order); 32 the owner record's copy on this chain not yet synced, so no owner signature can be checked here.

receiveMint.does: Completes a Circle transfer whose mint only this contract may complete, and counts it: a burn by a member of the strategy adds to what was received from it, any other burn is accepted uncounted.
checks: The message is a burn sent to Circle's TokenMessenger, on this chain's domain, naming this contract as the caller and the recipient.
Circle accepts it (attestation, nonce).
Exactly the amount less Circle's fee arrived.

params.message: Circle's CCTP V2 message of the burn, as attested.

report.does: Sends this leg's report to its hub: its holdings (as `holdings` reads them: in unified mode HyperCore's spot balance is what is available, so the perp's margin is counted once, in DEX 0's account value; measured exact in both account modes), its money sent to and received from each member, Circle's fees on them, a sequence number and the time and block observed. Directly on the same chain, else by a Circle message at standard finality; it reverts as Circle does.
checks: DEX 0 can be read.

holdings.does: The report's figures as a view, for a hub on this chain. In order: the holdings (USD: DEX 0's account value less the strategy's perp at its mark, so every other DEX 0 position counts at its mark, plus spot USDC and the USDC held on HyperEVM; and the perp's size as its asset, both in 18 decimals); what this contract sent to each member; what it received from each (USDC, 6 decimals); the current block; the block of its last move between HyperEVM and HyperCore; its operation count; and `tracked`, always false, since the agent trades this account without calling this contract. In unified mode HyperCore's spot balance is what is available, so the perp's margin is counted once, in DEX 0's account value, as in standard mode: measured exact in both account modes. Reverts if DEX 0 cannot be read.

returns.1: The leg's holdings now, each an asset and an amount, as its report to the hub carries them.
returns.2: What this contract has sent to each other contract of the strategy, gross, by link (0 the hub).
returns.3: What it has received from each other contract of the strategy, gross, by link.
returns.4: The block number of this reading.
returns.5: The block of its last move between HyperEVM and HyperCore (0 for a leg with none).
returns.6: How many counted calls it has made (`opCount`): the hub sees a move between two readings.
returns.7: Whether every change of its holdings goes through its own counted calls, so the hub may read it alone.

scheduleUpgrade.does: Schedules the strategy's upgrade to the version whose manifest the owner signed (`UpgradeStrategy(hub, chainId, manifest, nonce, deadline)`): the hub's code moves 24 hours later, its legs follow. A leg refuses it (`Unsupported`): the hub is the strategy's home.
scheduleUpgrade.who: The owner, by one credential's signature; anyone may submit it.
scheduleUpgrade.when: Any time, an exit included; refused while any action (an upgrade or a profile switch) is pending.
checks: The signature is the named credential's, at its own vault nonce, before the deadline (`BadSignature`, `Expired`).
The manifest is listed on this chain's registry at a version above the hub's, with a hub implementation (`NotListed`).
No action is pending (`AlreadyPending`), and the credential's removal is not pending (`RemovalPending`).

params.manifest: The version's manifest: the keccak of every member type's (type, domain, implementation, code hash) in it, the same bytes on every chain.
params.credential: The signing credential's id, `keccak256(abi.encode(kind, x, y))` as the deposit contract keys it: it must be the credential that signed, and its own vault nonce is spent.
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds.
params.signature: One owner credential's signature, in the deposit contract's "DLTX Owner" domain (no chain id): `0x01 ‖ r ‖ s ‖ v` for a wallet, or `0x02 ‖ x ‖ y ‖` the ABI-encoded WebAuthn assertion for a passkey.

cancelPendingAction.does: Cancels the pending upgrade or profile switch it names, exactly (`CancelPendingAction(hub, chainId, kind, target, due, deadline)`). A leg refuses it (`Unsupported`): the hub is the strategy's home.
cancelPendingAction.who: Any credential of the owner in effect; no nonce. Anyone may submit it.
cancelPendingAction.when: Until the action is applied, after its due time included.
checks: One credential in effect signed it, before the deadline.
An action of that kind, target and due time is pending (`NotPending`).

params.target: What it names: the version's manifest, or the profile.
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds.
params.signature: One owner credential's signature, in the deposit contract's "DLTX Owner" domain (no chain id): `0x01 ‖ r ‖ s ‖ v` for a wallet, or `0x02 ‖ x ‖ y ‖` the ABI-encoded WebAuthn assertion for a passkey.

applyUpgrade.does: Applies the due upgrade: the hub's code moves to the version's hub implementation, then it tells every leg (the one beside it by a direct `followUpgrade`, the one on another chain by Circle). Nothing else moves: no money, no position, no fee. A leg refuses it (`Unsupported`): the hub is the strategy's home.
applyUpgrade.when: Once the upgrade is due, outside the money lock; allowed during an exit.
checks: An upgrade is pending (`NotPending`) and due (`NotDue`).
Its scheduling credential still stands in the deposit contract and has no removal pending: otherwise the schedule is cleared instead (`ActionCleared`).
A leg on another chain that Circle cannot reach now is logged (`UpgradePending`): `publishUpgrade` resends it.

publishUpgrade.does: Sends the hub's current manifest, with a fresh publication time, to leg `k`: a leg created after its hub moved, or whose message expired or met a version its chain had not listed yet, catches up. A leg refuses it (`Unsupported`): the hub is the strategy's home.
publishUpgrade.when: Any time. Reverts as Circle (or the leg) does.

params.k: The leg, by its index among the hub's links.

followUpgrade.does: A leg on the hub's chain follows the hub's upgrade: it resolves the manifest on its own chain's registry and moves to that version's implementation of its member type; a version not above its own is ignored.
followUpgrade.who: The strategy's hub beside it (its link 0, on this chain), in the transaction that moved it.
checks: The caller is this leg's link 0 on this chain (`NotAllowed`).
The manifest is listed on this chain (`NotListed`).

followMessage.does: A leg on another chain than its hub follows the hub's `.upgrade.v1` message: ignored when published before this leg's creation, at or before its last applied upgrade, or more than 3 days ago; otherwise it resolves the manifest on this chain's registry and moves to that version's implementation (a manifest not listed here reverts, so the message waits, relayable).
followMessage.who: Circle's message transmitter, delivering the hub's finalized message (any other caller is refused).

pendingAction.does: The pending action: its kind (0 none, 1 an upgrade, 2 a profile switch), due time, scheduling credential and target.

returns.kind: 0 none, 1 an upgrade, 2 a profile switch.

MEMBER_TYPE.does: This implementation's member type: 1 the hub, 2 the Aave V3 asset leg, 3 the Hyperliquid leg.

exitModule.does: The first exit module (`HyperCoreLegExit`: `exitStep`, `bridgeOut`), its code hash checked when the implementation was deployed.

exitModuleB.does: The second exit module (`HyperCoreLegExitB`: the owner's exit order, the sweep, the status, the profile check, `receiveMint`, `report`, `holdings`), its code hash checked when the implementation was deployed.

profile.does: The asset profile this leg was created on: its perp and asset id are that profile's short part, which a profile switch keeps.

checkProfile.does: The short's part of an asset profile, checked on HyperEVM when the registry accepts it and at this leg's creation: a DEX 0 perp whose `perpAssetInfo` coin and size decimals are the profile's, the underlying that coin, the short's asset id `keccak256("dltx.asset." ‖ coin)`. Reverts `BadProfile` otherwise.

AgentProposed.does: An agent was proposed for the account: DLTX's (`proposeAgent`), or the owner's other than the burner.

params.effectiveAt: When it may be applied, as a Unix time in seconds: at once for the account's first agent, otherwise 24 hours after the proposal.

AgentSet.does: This contract approved a new agent on HyperCore, replacing the previous one: DLTX's applied, the owner's applied, the burner named by the owner, or the burner at the exit's start.

AgentCancelled.does: An owner credential cancelled the pending agents: DLTX's proposal and the owner's own choice.

DexWatched.does: A HIP-3 DEX joined the exit's watched list.

UpgradeSent.does: The hub told leg `link` of its version (directly beside it, or by Circle).

UpgradePending.does: The hub could not tell leg `link` now (Circle refused, or the leg is not yet created): `publishUpgrade` resends it.

errors.TooEarly: An agent was applied before its 24 hours, or the same token's residue was swept again within 20 blocks.
errors.NoCoreAccount: `applyAgent` was called before the contract's HyperCore account exists (its first `toMargin` creates it).
errors.NoAgent: An agent named or proposed is the zero address, or there is no pending agent to apply.
errors.BadAsset: The exit named a perp index of 10,000 or more; an owner order's asset or `szDecimals` is invalid, or it buys on spot; or the token swept is not pinned or has no residue.
errors.NotResidue: `sweepResidue` was called while the exit is not recovered with residue.
errors.NotOwnerWallet: The address is not an owner wallet credential on this chain, or for the sweep, `proposeSweep` did not see it at least 24 hours ago.
errors.BadParams: `validateParams` refused the parameters: a perp outside DEX 0, an asset that is zero or USD, or a bound, fee cap or fee budget outside its range.

contracts.name: StrategyFactory
contracts.title: The combination factory, version 1
contracts.brief: Creates a strategy's hub and legs as owner-upgradeable proxies on the version and asset profile you signed.
contracts.summary: One factory for every version and every asset profile, at the same address on each chain it serves; your deposit contract trusts it at once (its pinned vault factory). It pins the topology (the hub on Arbitrum, an Aave V3 asset leg on Arbitrum, a Hyperliquid leg on HyperEVM) and each contract's parameter type, but no code: your signed `CreateVault` names a version's manifest, and this chain's registry gives each contract's code from it. Each contract is the same fixed proxy, at an address that never depends on code. It refuses a version not listed here or not checked in, members naming different asset profiles, a profile not open here, and any configuration you did not sign. It holds no money and has no owner.

registry.does: This chain's registry: the factory hands it to every contract it creates, which reads its execution group's key, its check-ins and DLTX's fee address from it.

createVaultType.does: The whole typed-data type of `CreateVault` this factory accepts, composed at deployment from its pins: the primary type, then each member type once, sorted by name. The owner's authorisation of a strategy, an EIP-712 typed message a wallet shows field by field (amendment 2d): `CreateVault(address factory,bytes32 strategyId,uint8 group,uint32 hubDomain,StrategyHub hub,AaveV3Leg leg1,HyperCoreLeg leg2,uint256 deadline)`, each member's parameters a nested struct named by its type: `StrategyHub(uint16 fastFeeCapBp,uint16 feeBudgetBp,uint16 feeRateBp)`, `AaveV3Leg(address pool,address oracle,address weth,address usdc,address swapPool,address receiver,uint64 healthFloor,uint16 oracleBoundBp,uint16 dailyLossBp,uint16 fastFeeCapBp)`, `HyperCoreLeg(uint32 perp,bytes32 asset,uint16 orderBoundBp,uint16 fastFeeCapBp,uint16 feeBudgetBp)`. Signed in the owner's domain (`DLTX Owner`, version 1, the deposit contract as verifying contract, no chain id). `perp` is Hyperliquid's market index (1 is ETH), `asset` the hash `keccak256("dltx.asset.ETH")`.

create.does: Creates every one of a strategy's contracts that lives on this chain (the hub if its chain is this one, and each leg whose chain is), all in this one transaction, from a configuration the owner signed. Returns their addresses in order, the hub first when it is here.
create.who: Anyone may submit it: the owner's `CreateVault` signature is what authorises it.
create.when: Before the signature's deadline, once on each chain the strategy uses. On HyperEVM, only once the owner's deposit contract there has received the owner record, since it verifies the signature.
checks: The deadline has not passed.

The configuration names this factory, exactly as many legs as it pins, a hub chain it allows and an execution group the registry has (0 to 15) and that is not stopped on this chain (a key set, checked in within 7 days).
Each leg's code, chain and role match the factory's pin for that leg, in order.

The hub's parameters, if the hub is created here, and each local leg's parameters are checked by their own code (its bounds and its pinned protocols); a leg on another chain is checked when it is created there.
At least one of the strategy's contracts lives on this chain.
Each member's parameters are exactly as many 32-byte words as its type has fields, so no extra bytes can change the configuration without changing what was signed.

The owner is a contract, and one of its credentials in effect on this chain signed `CreateVault` over exactly this configuration (`createDigest`): every parameter of every member, typed field by field, in the owner's domain.
Each contract is created at its own fixed address, which can hold only one: creating it a second time reverts.

params.owner: The owner's deposit contract: the same address on every chain, and the one whose signature is checked.
params.cfg: The strategy's configuration (`StrategyConfig`): this factory, the execution group, the hub's chain and parameters, and each leg's code, chain, role and parameters. The owner signed every one of its fields (`CreateVault`).
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds: the call reverts after it.
params.signature: One of the owner's credentials' signature over `createDigest`: `0x01 ‖ r ‖ s ‖ v` for a wallet, or `0x02 ‖ x ‖ y ‖` the ABI-encoded WebAuthn assertion for a passkey.

createDigest.does: The digest the owner signs for a configuration (`CreateVault`, typed field by field): its factory, strategy id, execution group, hub chain, each member's parameters as a nested struct of its type, and the deadline, in the owner's domain. A wallet's `eth_signTypedData_v4` of the same message gives the same digest. Returns the EIP-712 digest.
checks: The configuration has as many legs as the factory pins, and each member's parameters are exactly its type's field count in 32-byte words (`BadConfig`).

params.owner: The owner's deposit contract: the typed message's verifying contract.
params.deadline: When the signature expires, as a Unix time in seconds.

authorisedFor.does: What the deposit contract asks before it funds an address: the owner, the strategy id and the configuration hash of a hub this factory created on this chain. Zeros for anything else, a leg included, so money enters a strategy at its hub only.

params.vault: The address the deposit contract is asked to fund.

returns.owner: The owner's deposit contract, or zero if the address is not a hub this factory created here.
returns.configHash: The hash of the configuration the owner signed, or zero.

memberOf.does: Any of the strategy's contracts this factory created on this chain: its owner, strategy id, configuration hash and position in the strategy. Zeros for any other address, so a zero owner tells them apart from a hub.

returns.owner: The owner's deposit contract, or zero if this factory did not create the address here.
returns.configHash: The hash of the configuration the owner signed.
returns.index: Its position in the strategy: 0 the hub, then 1 onward the legs in the configuration's order.

memberAddresses.does: Every one of a strategy's contracts' addresses, the hub first, on every chain, created yet or not: this factory has the same address on each chain, so each contract's address follows from the strategy id, the owner and the configuration alone. It does not check the configuration against the factory's pins.

params.cfg: The strategy's configuration (`StrategyConfig`), as the owner signs it.

returns.members: The addresses in order: the hub, then each leg in the configuration's order.
returns.configHash: The configuration's hash, the one the owner signs in `CreateVault`.

hubDomains.does: The chains a hub of this factory may live on, by Circle's CCTP domain number (Ethereum 0, Avalanche 1, OP Mainnet 2, Arbitrum 3, Base 6, Polygon 7, HyperEVM 19). Each is a chain where the deposit contract lives.

hubSetup.does: What a hub created here reads at its creation: each leg's value kind, in leg order.

legCount.does: How many legs this factory pins: 2 to 4. A strategy of this factory has exactly that many.

leg.does: The factory's pin of one leg (`LegPin`): its code, the code hash it must have, its chain (CCTP domain), its role (1 long, 2 short) and how its value is known (1 read on chain, 2 reported). Reverts beyond the last leg.

params.i: The leg's position, from 0: leg `i` is the strategy's contract number `i + 1`, after the hub.

PROXY_INIT_CODE_HASH.does: The keccak of the shared proxy's init code: in every member's address.

memberAt.does: The member at `salt`: `CREATE2(this factory, salt, the proxy's init-code hash)`.

proxyImplementation.does: What the proxy's constructor asks: the implementation staged for the member being created; zero outside a creation.

MemberCreated.does: One of a strategy's contracts was created and initialised.

params.configHash: The hash of the configuration the owner signed.
params.index: Its position in the strategy: 0 the hub, then 1 onward the legs in the configuration's order.

errors.ZeroAddress: At deployment, the registry or the hub code is zero.
errors.BadPins: At deployment, a pin is malformed: no hub chain or more than six, one named twice, or one that is not a deposit chain; fewer than two legs or more than four; a leg with no code, an unknown role or value kind, or a chain that is not a deposit chain; on this chain, a code whose hash differs from its pin or a leg code that does not declare the pinned role and value kind; a price source on a chain no hub may use, for no asset or for USD, with no feed, a zero maximum age, an unknown kind, an asset pinned twice or more than eight on one chain; a sequencer feed pinned twice or zero, or none for a rollup hub chain (OP Mainnet, Arbitrum, Base); or, on this chain, a feed with no code.
errors.BadConfig: The configuration does not match the factory: another factory, a different number of legs, a hub chain it does not allow, an execution group the registry does not have, or a leg whose code, chain or role is not its pin's.
errors.WrongChain: None of the strategy's contracts lives on this chain.
errors.BadSignature: The owner is not a contract, or no credential of the owner in effect on this chain signed this `CreateVault`.
errors.DeployFailed: A contract could not be created at its address, most often because it already exists there.
errors.BadOwner: The owner cannot answer `removalPendingOf` (an older deposit account): its strategy could never be upgraded nor switched.

contracts.name: StrategyRegistry
contracts.title: The strategy registry, version 1
contracts.brief: One per chain: the execution keys and their check-ins per version, the allowed versions and asset profiles, DLTX's fee address.
contracts.summary: One per chain, at the same address everywhere. It holds the execution key of each of sixteen groups, their check-ins per version and whether a group is stopped on a version (7 days without a check-in opens that version's escape hatch); the list of allowed versions (each a number, a manifest of every member's code on every chain, and the implementations living here) and the list of allowed asset profiles, both appended only by DLTX's recovery key behind 7 public days, a profile's facts checked on this chain when it is accepted, but for version 1 and the first asset profiles (ETH, BTC), which its constructor lists at once: its address, the same on every chain, is the hash of them; and DLTX's fee address. Neither DLTX nor the recovery key can move a strategy: an owner's signature does. It holds no money.

GROUPS.does: How many execution groups the registry holds, numbered from 0. Each group has its own key and its own check-in clock; a strategy names its group at creation.

STOP_AFTER.does: How long a group's key may go without checking in before the group counts as stopped and anyone may begin the exit of its strategies' contracts on this chain.

recovery.does: DLTX's offline recovery key on this chain: it sets the groups' keys, proposes the fee address and hands itself over.

pendingRecovery.does: A successor the recovery key proposed, not yet accepted (zero if none).

executionKey.does: One group's execution key on this chain (zero until the recovery key sets one). Each of the group's contracts reads it at every call, so a replacement applies to all of them at once.

lastCheckIn.does: When one group last checked in, as a Unix time in seconds: set when its first key is set, then at each check-in. Zero for a group never given a key.

feeAddress.does: DLTX's fee address on this chain: the only place a hub here pays DLTX's performance fee, read at the moment of payment. Zero until one is accepted; meanwhile a hub defers its charges, and an exit forgives the fee due on it.

pendingFeeAddress.does: A fee address the recovery key proposed, not yet accepted (zero if none).

setExecutionKey.does: Sets or replaces one group's execution key on this chain. Every contract of that group follows the new key at once.
checks: The group exists (0 to 15).
A non-zero key.

The group's first key starts its check-in clock. A replacement is not itself a check-in, but the recovery key can name a key it holds, which then checks in: the escape hatch protects against a DLTX that has gone, not against its recovery key. Your own `BeginExit` needs neither.

checkIn.does: Resets one group's 7-day clock, so the group is not stopped.
checkIn.who: The group's current execution key only. A key an owner revoked on one of their contracts still checks in for the group.
checkIn.when: Daily, whatever the group's strategies need. A check-in after the group stopped makes it not stopped again; a contract whose exit has already begun stays in exit.

params.versions: The versions the group still supports.

stopped.does: Whether a group has gone 7 days or more without a check-in, or was never given a key. Anyone may then begin the exit of any of the group's contracts on this chain.

proposeRecovery.does: Proposes the recovery key's successor; zero withdraws a proposal.

params.next: The proposed successor recovery key; zero withdraws a pending proposal.

acceptRecovery.does: The proposed successor takes over as the recovery key.
acceptRecovery.who: The proposed successor only, proving it is controlled.

proposeFeeAddress.does: Proposes this chain's next fee address; zero withdraws a proposal. The fee address does not change until the proposed address accepts.

params.next: The proposed fee address; zero withdraws a pending proposal.

acceptFeeAddress.does: The proposed fee address accepts and becomes this chain's fee address, so fees never go to an address nobody controls.

LISTING_DELAY.does: How long a proposed version or profile is public before recovery may accept it: 7 days.

MAX_SUCCESSIONS.does: The most registry successions between this registry and a listed implementation's own listing registry: 8.

PROFILE_OPEN.does: `profileState`: accepted, open to new strategies and switches.

PROFILE_CLOSED.does: `profileState`: closed to new strategies; strategies that stored it keep it.

predecessor.does: The registry this one succeeds (zero for the first): a version naming this registry, or a registry descending from it by at most `MAX_SUCCESSIONS` predecessors, may be listed.

firstVersion.does: This registry's first version number (1 for the first registry).

firstKeyAt.does: When a group's first key was set: its check-in clock starts there.

latestVersion.does: The highest accepted version (0 before any).

acceptedAt.does: When a version was accepted: its check-in clock for every group starts there.

versionOf.does: A manifest's version (0: not listed here).

implementation.does: A version's implementation of a member type on this chain (zero: none here).

params.memberType: 1 the hub, 2 the Aave V3 asset leg, 3 the Hyperliquid leg.

localTypes.does: The member types of a version that live on this chain.

proposal.does: A pending version's proposal: its due time, manifest, and local member types and implementations.

proposeVersion.does: Proposes a version with every member type of it on every chain; the manifest is computed here. Each member type living on this chain must name an implementation with that code hash, whose `CODE_VERSION` is the number, whose `MEMBER_TYPE` is its own, and whose listing registry is this one or a later registry descending from it (each naming the one before as its predecessor, at most `MAX_SUCCESSIONS` steps). Public for 7 days.
checks: The number is above the latest and not already proposed (`BadVersion`).
The members are strictly ordered by type, each named; at least one lives here (`BadVersion`).
Each local implementation has the code hash named (`CodeChanged`) and answers as above (`BadVersion`).
The manifest is not already listed (`BadVersion`).

params.members: Every member type of the version: (type, CCTP domain, implementation, code hash), by type.

withdrawVersion.does: Withdraws a pending version proposal (a defect found in the 7 days).

acceptVersion.does: Lists a proposed version once its 7 days have passed, in version order, every local code hash unchanged; seeds its check-in clock for every group.
checks: Proposed (`BadVersion`), due (`NotDue`), the next number (`BadVersion`), every code hash unchanged (`CodeChanged`).

proposeProfile.does: Proposes an asset profile's full data; its id is the data's hash. Public for 7 days.
checks: Not already known (`AlreadyPending`).

acceptProfile.does: Accepts a proposed profile once its 7 days have passed: every fact of it living on this chain is checked by the latest version's implementation of each member type here (`checkProfile`); then it is open to new strategies.
checks: Proposed (`BadProfile`) and due (`NotDue`); a version is listed (`BadVersion`); each local implementation's check passes (`BadProfile`).

closeProfile.does: Closes an open profile to new strategies and to switches; every strategy that stored it keeps its copy.

profileOpen.does: Whether a profile is open to new strategies.

profileOf.does: A profile's data (proposed, open or closed); zeros for an unknown id.

profileIds.does: Every accepted profile's id, in order of acceptance.

profileState.does: A profile's state: 0 unknown, 1 proposed, 2 open, 3 closed.

profileDue.does: When a proposed profile may be accepted.

ExecutionKeySet.does: A group's execution key was set or replaced.

params.previous: The key it replaced (zero for the group's first).

params.at: When, as a Unix time in seconds.

RecoveryProposed.does: The recovery key proposed a successor (or withdrew a proposal, with zero).

params.proposed: The proposed successor; zero withdraws a proposal.

RecoverySet.does: A proposed successor accepted and is now the recovery key.

FeeAddressProposed.does: The recovery key proposed a new fee address (or withdrew a proposal, with zero).

params.current: The fee address now (zero if none).
params.proposed: The proposed fee address; zero withdraws a proposal.

FeeAddressSet.does: A proposed fee address accepted and is now this chain's fee address.

params.previous: The fee address it replaced (zero for the first).

ProfileAccepted.does: A profile is open to new strategies.

ProfileClosed.does: A profile is closed to new strategies.

errors.ZeroAddress: An address that must be set is zero: the recovery key at deployment, or a new execution key.
errors.NotAllowed: The caller may not make this call: not the recovery key, not the group's current execution key (or no such group), or not the proposed address accepting.
errors.BadGroup: The execution group is 16 or more: the registry holds groups 0 to 15.
errors.BadVersion: A version proposal or acceptance out of order, malformed, or naming an implementation that does not answer as its version; a check-in of a version not accepted.
errors.AlreadyPending: The profile is already proposed or known.
errors.CodeChanged: An implementation's code hash differs from the one proposed.
errors.BadProfile: The profile is not in the state the call needs.
